summary: Compose qualified MAX image, gallery and supported-video publication through the released-upload worker bridge.

impacts.evidence: Media scope is derived from the host-owned connector account and released-upload gate.
Media bytes remain in upload storage and are not copied to canonical events or audit.
The existing provider-neutral SocialPublishRequest and worker dispatch are reused.
No event envelope or event payload changes.
UploadRequest gains callback-scoped access-token material required by the documented MAX upload endpoint; it is not normalized or persisted.
Existing upload release records, social publication state and receipts are reused.
Upload URLs use an exact host allowlist and multipart requests are bounded before egress.
Existing social publication lifecycle and connector capability settings remain mandatory.
Existing publication and receipt lineage covers the media write without storing media contents.
The upload/send sequence has no complete caller idempotency key; existing receipt recovery handles ambiguous outcomes.
The host transport adds fixed-host multipart upload egress under the existing outbound policy.
Existing worker leases, retry/DLQ, timeout and MAX rate policy remain active.
Disabling media/video capability admission or upload processing stops new media publication without migration.
Deterministic host allowlist, multipart, adapter and worker mapping tests cover success and malformed media cases.
